### Orientation

> Counts below: Crossref journal-article records of this journal published 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (277 records; 243, or 88%, carry an abstract); a record is counted when the regex matches its title or abstract. Percentages use 243 as the denominator, so they are lower bounds for the 34 records without an abstract. Regexes are word-boundary patterns written out in the Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics tables. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Theoretical. "argue", "defend", "thesis" or "objection" appear in 173 of 243 abstracts (71.2%; regex `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*`). Reading the 2 abstracts that mention participants showed one study with participant data (https://doi.org/10.1111/nous.12492) and one non-empirical use |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Neither is a method here. The 5 "quantitative/statistical" hits and 3 "qualitative" hits were read: all are philosophical uses (statistical evidence in legal reasoning, qualitative hedonism, statistical physics) and none is a quantitative or qualitative study |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Present through logic, mathematics, physics and cognitive science content: formal terms 19.8% (48), "probability/Bayesian/decision theory" 13.6% (33), "scientific/explanation/physics/quantum/spacetime" 15.6% (38), "neuroscience/cognitive science/psychology" 5.8% (14) of 243 abstracts. The publisher keyword list (overview page copy 2023-09-28) names linguistic, cognitive and consciousness topics |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope statement is available: the journal aims to publish articles that make "standalone, substantial contributions" across the breadth of philosophy and its history (https://web.archive.org/web/20250528082557/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/14680068, Wayback copy dated 2025-05-28). No required theoretical framing is stated there; the same text says no particular methodology is required. Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** The overview copy of 2023-09-28 names "long critical studies of important books" as an accepted form alongside articles (https://web.archive.org/web/20230928161155/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14680068/homepage/productinformation.html). Observed practice: 173 of 243 abstracts (71.2%) use argue, defend, thesis or objection language (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Article type and length**: observed median 21 pages with quartiles 16 and 26 over 243 records with a page range (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0029-4624/works). The word limit and structure rules are unreadable (see Format).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No page read states what happens to out-of-scope submissions.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref journal-article records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 whose title or abstract matches the regex, over the 243 records with an abstract (88% of 277). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Where I read the hits and they were not uses of the method, the score is set from the hits actually read and the row says so. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 1 | Participant data appear in 1 record I read (https://doi.org/10.1111/nous.12492, an evidence-from-the-field study of happiness and well-being concepts); regex `\bparticipants\b\|\bsurvey\w*\|\bvignette\w*` gives 2 of 243 (0.8%), one of which is a non-empirical use. The 5 "quantitative/statistical" hits were read and none is a quantitative study |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | Regex `\bqualitative\b\|\binterview\w*\|\bethnograph\w*\|\bthematic analysis\b` gives 3 of 243 (1.2%); all 3 were read and are philosophical uses of "qualitative" (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1111/nous.12527) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Regex `\bautoethnograph\w*\|\bethnograph\w*` gives 0 of 243 abstracts (and 0 titles of 277) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*` 173 of 243 (71.2%); `\bconceptual\w*\|\banalysis of\b\|\baccount of\b\|\btheory of\b` 81 of 243 (33.3%) |
| Formal / logical proof (added row) | 3 | `\btheorem\w*\|\bprove[sd]?\b\|\bproof\w*\|\bformal (?:model\|framework\|semantics\|system)\w*\|\bmodel-theor\w*\|\baxiom\w*` 16 of 243 (6.6%); the broader logic/formal pattern 48 of 243 (19.8%) |
| Mixed methods | 0 | `\bmixed[- ]method\w*` 0 of 243 |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | `\bsystematic review\w*\|\bmeta-analys\w*\|\bscoping review\w*` 0 of 243 |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: Crossref abstract-based counts 4 (277 records, 88% with abstract; regexes written out); OpenAlex group-by counts 4; publisher metrics and aims (Wayback copies, 2024-03-10 to 2025-05-28) 3; journal-specific policies and guidelines 0 (page unreadable, no archive copy); experiential layer 3 (APA Journal Survey Project n=394 voluntary and self-selected; SciRev n=2).

**What the APA survey is**: the APA Journal Survey Project (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/733) aggregates voluntary submissions by authors. The figures used are the all-years aggregate on the page, retrieved 2026-11-23; the sample is self-selected and includes unfiltered years, so acceptance shares may not describe current practice.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Unknown submission rules**: the word limit, anonymisation wording and ethics rules are unreadable (Format, Identity). A manuscript should be checked against the live guidelines before submission; nothing here can be relied on for those rules.
- **AI use**: undisclosed substantial generative AI use, or AI-altered evidential images, breaches the publisher policy (AI Policy, https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/article/ai-guidelines/).
- **Method fit**: empirical or participant-data studies are almost absent (1 record in 243 abstracts, Methodological Preferences). This is a frequency, not a stated rule; the journal says no particular methodology is required.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: publisher-reported first decision 58 days (2023) to 67 days; survey respondents average 3.2 months to a verdict and 12.4 months to publication (Review Cycle Time). SciRev n=2 reports 4.4 months total handling for accepted manuscripts.
- **Competition**: publisher-reported acceptance rate 8% (2023) and 9% (2025 snapshot); survey respondents report 2.79% of 394 initial verdicts as acceptances (11); the survey's 10.91% "overall acceptance rate" also counts 32 later acceptances, (11 + 32) / 394 (Metrics). These numbers imply that most submissions are rejected.
- **Feedback**: only 141 of 394 survey entries carry comments, and a SciRev review quotes a rejection email saying rejected papers get no comments (Practical Concerns), so a rejection may come without reviewer text.
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted version is delayed 24 months for humanities and social science journals under the publisher page (Preprint Policy); gold access lists an APC of USD 2900 per OpenAlex, unverified.

### Best Suited For

- Argument-driven analytic papers: 71.2% of abstracts use argue, defend, thesis or objection language (Methodological Preferences), and epistemology (33.7%), ethics (20.2%), logic and formal work (19.8%) and metaphysics (15.6%) are the largest topic groups (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Single-author work: 76% of records with an author list are single-author (Voice & Style).
- Formal or technical contributions in logic, probability or philosophy of physics: formal terms 19.8%, probability and decision theory 13.6%, physics and scientific-explanation terms 15.6% (Subject Density).

### Not Recommended For

- Empirical, participant-based or qualitative studies: 1 of 243 abstracts is a participant-data study (Methodological Preferences). The count shows rarity, not rejection.
- Work centred on continental, decolonial, non-Western or applied political topics: phenomenology and continental names 1.6%, non-Western terms 0.4%, politics, war and violence terms 0% (Sensitive Topics). Again a frequency, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors who need a published, verified word limit or anonymisation rule before choosing: those rules are unreadable here (Format, Identity).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus (general philosophy, analytic orientation); they are not a claim about acceptance odds, and no fit evidence was collected for them in this pass.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Philosophical Studies](philosophical-studies.md) | General-philosophy scope; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [Mind](mind.md) | General-philosophy scope; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [Philosophy and Phenomenological Research](philosophy-and-phenomenological-research-ppr.md) | General-philosophy scope; an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
